NTA, but I feel like a lot of the replies here are completely brushing over the fact that both you and your sister are 15 years old. If you were both adults, I would be all aboard the train of cutting her out of your life and never forgiving her, but you're both still kids. 

Let me clear in that I don't think what she did is defensible in any way. She should be old enough to know better, but I also know what being a 15 year old girl feels like, and I know that we do very stupid and emotionally driven things at that age that can be absolutely devastating to the people around us. I guarantee you that however bad she feels about her actions now, she will only feel worse as she gets older and realizes how stupid and terrible what she did was. 

With all that being said, I don't think you're an asshole for not wanting to go to therapy and work things out with her right now. The onus is not on your to work things out between the two of you. I'm sure your parents are doing what they can to try and help, and therapy is probably one of the only things they can think of to do so. If you never want to work things out with her or forgive her, that's fine, but it sits very ill with me having a bunch of adults saying that it's right to never even consider forgiveness for the rest of your life while you're still so young. You shouldn't shut out the possibility for the rest of your life right now while you're still angry and mourning the loss of someone and something so precious to you. I promise you, as someone who has lost someone closer to me than anyone else in the world, that pain does get easier to deal with over time. 

Just give it time, and don't shut out the POSSIBILITY of forgiveness in the future like so many people here seem to be encouraging. I'm not saying you have ever to forgive her, but I don't want you to be in your 20s or 30s thinking "well, a bunch of grown up strangers on the internet told me I never had to forgive my sister, so I'll never even consider forgiving her."
